ALKA SARIN, J. (Oral)
1.
The parties are being referred to as driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle, Insurance Company and the claimants for the sake of clarity.
2. Since the facts, as recorded in the impugned award passed by the Tribunal, are not in dispute, the same are not being reproduced herein for the sake of brevity.
3. Firstly, the appeals filed by the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle are being taken up.

. Learned counsel for the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle would contend that there was a cover-note which was found in the car and also finds mentioned in the challan for the period 09.08.2012 to 2 of 11 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:166524 08.08.2013 and since the accident took place on 10.08.2012 and, hence, the period of the accident was covered.

The learned counsel Ashok Kumar vs Rameshwari Bai And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114416687/
2 would further contend that the claim petition itself was filed on 31.08.2012 and on 21.09.2012 a DDR was got registered by one Bharat Bhushan regarding loss of insurance cover-note book No.E-49872 having cover-notes Nos.31498712, 31498718 and 3149719.

sentences.text: The learned counsel would further contend that the said DDR was lodged in Faridabad and it was averred that the said cover-notes were forged and fabricated as the lost cover-notes were used to prepare the cover-note which has been relied upon by the driver- cum-owner of the offending vehicle.

The learned counsel would further contend that the accident took place in Kurukshetra and there is no explanation as to how a cover-note which is alleged to have been lost post the accident in Faridabad was used in Kurukshetra.

The leaned counsel has further referred to the statement of Jagdish Kumar, Senior Analyst, Legal Claims, Bharti Axa General Insurance Company New Delhi who had stepped into the witness box as RW2 and in his cross-examination he had stated that he did not know to whom the cover-note book was issued by the Insurance Company.

entities.text: Bharti Axa General Insurance Company New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He could also not disclose the names of the persons in whose names the remaining cover-notes of the above said book were issued.
He admitted that the cover-note (Ex.R1) did not bear any overwriting and cutting.
He also could not tell whether Bharat Bhushan was still an employee of the Insurance Company.
It is further the contention of the learned counsel that the said witness while stepping into the witness box as RW2 nowhere stated that the cover-note (Ex.R1) was a forged and fabricated document.
It 3 of 11 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:166524 is, hence, the contention of the learned counsel that the Insurance Company has erroneously been absolved.

5. Per contra, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company would contend that the Insurance Company has rightly been absolved since it has proved on record that the cover-notes were lost and a DDR was lodged regarding the same.

It is further the contention of the learned counsel that since the cover-note did not bear the seal of the Insurance Company and, hence, it has rightly been held by the Tribunal that the said document was not a genuine document.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties.
7. In the present case the accident took place on 10.08.2012.
The cover-note (Ex.R1) was covering the period from 09.08.2012 to 08.08.2013.
The challan which was produced on the record as Ex.P3 refers to the cover-note.

The learned counsel for the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle by way an application (CM-1234-CII-2015 in FAO-10528-2014) for additional evidence has produced on record Annexure P-3 which is a recovery memo dated 23.08.2012 which clearly refers that the cover-note No.31498719 dated 08.08.2012 had been recovered from the car.
The said was stated to have been taken into police custody.
Further still, the DDR which is alleged to have been registered by one Bharat Bhushan was lodged at Faridabad though the accident, in the present case, is stated to have taken place at Kurukshetra.

There is no co-relation or explanation as to how the cover-note which is alleged to have been lost in Faridabad on 20.09.2012 was used in an accident which occurred on 10.08.2012 and was recovered from a car in Kurukshetra.
The author of the DDR - Bharat Bhushan - did 4 of 11 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:166524 not step into the witness box for reasons best known to the Insurance Company.
RW2 Jagdish Kumar, Senior Analyst, Legal Claims who appeared on behalf of the Insurance Company did not mention in his statement that the document was forged and fabricated.
He only stated that a DDR had been registered regarding the lost cover-note and the Insurance Company had not received any premium on this cover-note.

sentences.text: He could not state whether the said Bharat Bhushan was still employed with the Insurance Company.
He also could not tell the names of the persons in whose names the remaining cover-notes of the said book were issued.
He admitted that there was no overwriting or cutting in Ex.R1, the cover-note.

Though it has been argued by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the cover-note did not bear the seal of the Insurance Company, however, that is not even mentioned in the statement made by RW2.
The Tribunal in the present case has not relied upon the cover-note only on the ground that the proof of premium was not produced and that the said document appeared to be a procured one.
Once the cover- note was produced by the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle, the onus shifted on to the Insurance Company to prove that the same was a forged and fabricated document.

In the evidence led by the Insurance Company it has not even been stated by the witness in his examination-in- chief that the said document was forged and fabricated.
8.
In view of the above, the findings returned by the Tribunal in the impugned award on issue No.3 cannot be sustained in law and the same 5 of 11 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:166524 are set aside.
Accordingly, issue No.3 is decided against the Insurance Company and it is held that the Insurance Company shall primarily be liable to pay the compensation.
9. No other point has been raised in these appeals.

Learned counsel for the claimants-parents of the deceased child would contend that the deceased child was about 02 years of age at the time of the accident and the amount of compensation as awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

Firstly, in support of his arguments the learned counsel has placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kusmi Devi vs. Mohd. Kasim & Anr. [2024 (1) PLR (49)] to contend that in an accident which took place in the year 1994 the Hon'ble Supreme Court had granted an amount of Rs.6,00,000/- as compensation in the case of death of a 3-year old child.

[2022 (1) RCR (Civil) 165] to contend that Hon'ble Supreme Court had taken the notional income as Rs.25,000/- per annum in a similar case where the accident took place in the year 2004.

11. Per contra, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company would contend that sufficient amount has already been awarded as 6 of 11 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:166524 compensation in the present case and that there is no scope of any enhancement.

Since the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a beneficial piece of legislation, the Courts are always inclined to see where the claimants can get maximum benefit within the four corners of the law as laid down.
15.

Though in the case of Kusumi Devi (supra), an amount of six lakhs was awarded by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, however, this Court is inclined to assess the income as per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kurvan Ansari @ Kurvan Ali (supra) by fixing a notional income for the deceased child.
The accident in the present case had taken place in the year 2012.
The accident in the case of Kurvan Ansari @ Kurvan Ali (supra) pertains to the year 2004.

For an accident which had taken place in the year 2004 their Lordships have assessed the notional income of the deceased as Rs.25,000/- per annum and applied a multiplier of '15' and also awarded funeral expenses and filial consortium.

Keeping in view the fact that the present accident had taken place in the year 7 of 11 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:166524 2012, this Court deems it appropriate to assess the notional income of the child as Rs.50,000/- per annum and multiplier of '15' would have to be applied since the deceased was a child of 2 years.
The claimants would also be entitled to funeral expenses of Rs.18,000/- and filial consortium of Rs.48,000/- each (being parents of the deceased).

Accordingly, the reworked compensation is as under :
Sr. Heads Compensation Awarded No.
 1 Notional income Rs.50,000/-
 2 Multiplier 15 Rs.7,50,000/- (Rs.50,000/- x 15)
 3 Funeral expenses Rs.18,000/- (Rs.15,000+20% increase)
 4. Loss of Consortium :
 (i) Filial Rs.96,000/- (48,000 x 2)
 5 Total Compensation Rs.8,64,000/-
16.

The amount in excess of and over and above the amount awarded by the Tribunal shall also attract interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the realization of the entire amount.
The amount shall be apportioned between the claimants as directed by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has not assessed her income which ought to have been assessed as per the minimum wages prevailing at the relevant point of time by applying the multiplier method keeping in view the disability of the claimant.
The learned counsel would further contend that the amounts awarded under the heads pain and suffering, special diet and transportation are also on the lower side.

19. Per contra, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company would contend that sufficient amount has already been awarded as compensation in the present case and that there is no scope of any enhancement.
20. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties.

21. In the present case, the claimant got examined Dr. Bimla Gouri as PW3 who had deposed that the claimant was a case of fracture humerus right side with fracture femur right side and her date of trauma was 10.08.2012 and her total disability assessed was 25% which was due to moderate restrictions of movements at right knee joint with swelling and mild restriction of movements at Ashok Kumar vs Rameshwari Bai And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114416687/

Keeping in view the deposition of PW3 - Dr. Bimla Gouri - this Court deems it fit to assess the bodily disability of the claimant @ 15%.
22. A housewife does much more than a single person can do.

Infact, a housewife performs multiple functions in the house i.e. cooking for the family, cleaning the house, washing cloths and utensils,
the list is endless.

Thus, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal ought to have assessed the monthly notional income of the claimant and ought to have applied multiplier method also so far as the bodily disability is concerned.

As stated above, keeping in view the multifarious functions of a housewife and the disability suffered by the claimant, her notional income is assessed as a skilled worker which at the relevant point of time was Rs.5,357/- per month.
Since the claimant at the time of the accident was 40 years of age, a multiplier of '15' is applicable.

Further, the amounts under the heads pain and suffering, special diet and transportation as awarded by the Tribunal are also on the lower side and this Court deems it appropriate to enhance the same to Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.10,000/- towards special diet and Rs.10,000/- towards transportation charges.
The amounts awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads are maintained.

The appeals being FAO Nos.10528 and 10529 of 2014 filed by the driver-cum-owner and the appeals being FAO Nos.709 and 2947 of 2015 filed by the claimants stand allowed.
